How to use the original audio controls
SOURCE\nUse MODE on the steering wheel or the source buttons on the original head unit to choose radio, CD, USB/iPod or AUX.

STATIONS\nUse AM/FM to choose a band, presets 1–6 to recall saved stations, and the tuning/seek controls to find a station. The steering-wheel CH buttons change presets. RDS settings are available for FM in MENU.

TRACKS AND DISCS\nUse SKIP/track buttons or steering-wheel CH to change tracks. Select the disc on the original head unit. For MP3/WMA discs, press SEL/ENTER to browse folders and files; turn to select, press to confirm. MENU → PLAY MODE offers repeat, random and scan. TITLE changes the displayed text.

TRACKS AND FOLDERS\nUse SKIP/track buttons or steering-wheel CH to change tracks. Press SEL/ENTER to browse folders and files; turn to select, press to confirm. MENU → PLAY MODE offers repeat, random and scan. TITLE changes the displayed text.

SONGS AND LIBRARY\nUse SKIP/track buttons or steering-wheel CH to change songs. Press SEL/ENTER to browse Playlists, Artists, Albums and Songs; turn to select, press to confirm. MENU → PLAY MODE offers shuffle and repeat. TITLE changes the displayed text.

AUDIO SETTINGS\nPress MENU on the original head unit. Turn SEL/ENTER to choose an item or change its value, and press to select/confirm. Use RETURN to go back. This includes bass, treble, balance/fader and SVC. Honda Box displays the received settings; use the car controls to adjust them.

Needed for climate panels, volume, source, track and vehicle menu overlays. Open the Android permission screen, allow Honda Box Service to display over other apps, then return here. Appears across the bottom of the screen when climate values change. Hides 5 seconds after the last change; tap to dismiss sooner. The gear on the right opens Honda Box settings. This switch only controls automatic large popups; it does not enable the compact bar. Use the vehicle controls to adjust the climate.

Works independently of automatic large popups. Stays centered at the bottom while the climate is on. If side buttons are enabled but hidden, tapping the open bar reveals them; when visible, tapping the bar or the right button minimizes it. Without side buttons, tapping the bar minimizes it directly. The translucent handle stays visible; tap it to reopen the bar. A climate change expands a folded bar and folds it again after 5 seconds. While the large panel is open, the compact bar waits underneath and its timer starts after that panel closes. Both bar and handle disappear when the climate is off.
Both panels follow the app theme. Each preview uses sample values for 15 seconds, without changing climate settings or the enabled options.

Checks periodically while the screen is on (minimum interval: 15 minutes; Android may delay it). No recovery after ACC OFF or a manual stop. Open Honda Box to resume after stopping.
FYT settings app was not found. Opening Android settings instead.
Choose the service, not the selector

Select Honda Box Service in startup and keep-alive lists. It starts in the background without opening a window. The separate Honda Box icon opens the source selector.\n\nIf the picker shows package names, choose com.crewbeat.hondabox. Do not add the Radio, CD or USB shortcuts as startup targets.

1. Open the head unit’s original FYT Settings app.
2. Go to User → Application Settings.
3. Add Honda Box Service to autostart after boot and after sleep. Enable both options if the firmware lists them separately.
4. If a separate keep-alive or background exception list exists, add the same service there. Autostart relaunches an app; keep-alive controls whether it may remain running.
5. In Honda Box → Settings → Background operation, leave boot/ignition startup and automatic recovery enabled.

Allow display over other apps for the climate, volume, source and track overlays. This permission is separate from autostart.\n\nAllow notifications if Android requests it; the running service uses a persistent notification. Use the battery settings button to allow unrestricted background operation or exclude Honda Box Service from battery optimisation. If the firmware has a separate background-start permission, allow it too. Menu names vary by Android version.
If the FYT menu is missing

Check the original FYT Settings app, not only Android Settings or the launcher preferences. The FYT button opens that app if installed; otherwise it opens Android Settings.\n\nSome firmware builds hide or omit startup management. Use the startup options actually available on your head unit. Honda Box cannot grant itself a vendor keep-alive exception. If the list is absent or startup still fails, note the firmware version and check boot and wake separately using the checklist.

Open DUDU Settings → Vehicle → Startup Settings. Depending on the version, this may be named Start up.

Add Honda Box Service under Apps to open at Startup. Add it to Sleep Mode Keep-Alive App / Keep alive as well, if available.

Some versions also offer Automatic Task: Vehicle ignition → Open app → Honda Box Service. A short delay, such as 5 seconds, can allow startup to settle. Use one startup mechanism first to avoid duplicate launches. These menu names and options vary by firmware; they are not present on every unit.

Installing DUDU Launcher does not by itself turn stock FYT firmware into DUDU OS. If Vehicle / Startup Settings is not present, use the stock FYT autostart instructions instead.\n\nIf your launcher offers its own startup or keep-alive list, choose Honda Box Service there. An Android battery exception alone does not replace the FYT startup list. The system-settings button opens the settings handler provided by Android; it does not jump directly to a DUDU-specific page.

Configure the startup list, then perform a real Android/head-unit restart. Merely turning the original audio off and on is not a cold boot.\n\nWait for Android and FYT to finish starting. Without opening a player, change the volume or climate and check an enabled overlay. Honda Box Service should run without bringing the source selector or a player to the foreground.

Switch ignition / ACC off and wait until the head unit actually enters deep sleep; the delay depends on the firmware. Switch ACC on again. A quick off/on may not test sleep at all.\n\nCheck that the service reconnects, the current-source overlay appears if enabled, and new volume/climate changes update. If data does not return, open Honda Box once: if this restores it, recheck the firmware startup target and background permissions.

Stop in Honda Box deliberately pauses automatic starts and cancels periodic recovery. Boot, ACC and the headless service icon do not undo that pause. Open the Honda Box interface to resume.\n\nThe recovery check is a fallback with a minimum repeat interval of 15 minutes, and Android can delay it. It is cancelled on ACC OFF and does not replace immediate firmware autostart. After a firmware force-stop, FYT may need to launch the service again.
What to check if it still fails

A player or selector opens at startup: select Honda Box Service instead of a UI shortcut.

The service runs but overlays are missing: allow display over other apps and enable the required overlays in Honda Box settings. Notification permission is separate.

It works after reboot but not after sleep: recheck the firmware’s wake/autostart and keep-alive lists.

The service runs but vehicle data is missing: check the FYT connection in Debug and the selected CAN profile. Keep-alive cannot fix a wrong vehicle profile or absent CAN data.

For a short diagnostic capture, open Settings → Diagnostics, reset the log, enable recording, reproduce the problem and export it. Turn recording off afterwards; normal use does not require continuous logging.
Pause Android media when leaving AUX

The default resumes only music that was playing when Honda Box paused it after leaving AUX. Already paused music stays paused. Requires a player that accepts Android media buttons. Reconnecting or waking the service does not start playback.

Apply Honda Accord (6291908) processing and workarounds to any CAN profile: climate power and DUAL, source and USB/iPod detection, media, menus and player controls. Off by default; native 6291908 processing is always enabled. The actual CAN profile is unchanged. Changing this setting reconnects the FYT service subscriptions.

Counts cover this connection, including when recording is off. Reset log keeps them; reconnect or profile change clears them. Missing packets do not mean unsupported hardware. FYT startup zero values do not confirm source or player support. Length is the last received payload length; receipt alone does not confirm decoding.
